about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Pit Stop, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_promises.py refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine. Copied from Windstorm Tardigrade's PROMISES.json (the Windstorm skill standard, 2026-11-22).
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be the codon's Proof in the plan.
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the plugin is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in an overnight stress test on a Linux laptop and an Intel Mac: a project-scope Pit Stop 0.6.1 in a test folder loaded the user-scope 0.1.4 instead; /hooks showed only 0.1.4's PreCompact hook, and nothing told the person. A session started with --plugin-dir pointing at 0.6.1 loaded 0.6.1 and no 0.1.4 hook: the start flag hides the older install; without the flag the older one wins. A restart is a second way to land on the older install: after a reboot the same session came back without its --plugin-dir flag and ran 0.1.4's hook again, with nothing said.
rows.promise: The checkup names an older Pit Stop install that wins over a newer one in another scope, and the one command that removes or updates the older.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22: two machines of ours have run Pit Stop 0.1.4 since 2026-11-10 while the release is 0.6.1. 0.1.4 predates setup's switch-on of marketplace auto-update (0.5.2), Claude Code leaves auto-update off for marketplaces other than Anthropic's (unset on both), and neither runs the fleet helper, so nothing moved them.
rows.promise: From the release that builds G13.1, every install tells its person once that a newer Pit Stop exists, with the command. Installs from before that are told by the README's 'Staying up to date' section; the two machines are updated with Claude Code's own plugin commands in the second wave of that test (2026-11-22), which is this row's proof.
rows.proven: 2026-11-22, on the two machines (a macOS test machine and a Linux laptop, main users, user scope, Claude Code 2.1.330): the README's two commands, typed word for word, moved Pit Stop 0.1.4 (85274eae) to 0.6.1 at 2330ee87, main's head at that minute, each with exit 0 and 'updated from 0.1.4 to 0.6.1 for scope user. Restart to apply changes.' Settings were unchanged and nothing was restarted. After a clean reboot of the macOS machine, every session that came back ran the new hooks (resume stamps that only the new code writes) with no hook error. The README's third step (/pit-stop setup, which switches the catalog's auto-update on) was not run, on purpose: with the './' entry it would let every merge to main reach those machines by itself (row P10). That step is to be seen with 0.6.2, once the catalog pins a release. This covers the second half of the promise; the notice of G13.1 is still to build.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, in a clean test account on a Mac: after setup --apply and claude plugin uninstall, autoUpdate true on the marketplace entry, pit-stop/config.json (auto_tune true), released.json, checkup/ and the cache folder all stayed.
rows.promise: setup.py --undo puts back what --apply and --fleet changed and names the history files it leaves.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, in a fresh test folder on a model with a 1M context (its status line read 1.00M): after one prompt the tuner wrote window 150K and idle point 100K and told the person 'idle point: 100K is the lowest Claude Code allows, and the right one for a 200K context'. It had guessed the limit from the folder's peak context, 38K. For a 1M model its own rules start at window 500K and idle point 200K.
rows.promise: The tuner takes the context limit from the model: a [1m] id or a list of models in optimize.py. When it cannot tell, it says so ('could not tell this model's context; assumed 200K; pass --context-limit') instead of stating a guess as a fact.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, on a Mac after a reboot: two sessions that had never taken a turn were brought back with claude --resume <id>; each printed 'No conversation found with session ID: …' and ended, so they were gone. The same restore dropped a working session's --plugin-dir flag. Pit Stop's own exit-and-resume (G15.1) is not built yet, so no install loses a session this way today; the row is dated with that build so that the gate refuses to ship it without the check.
rows.promise: Exit-and-resume exits only a session whose conversation exists, and starts it again with every flag it was started with.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, on a Mac: the hand-run optimize.py --apply ran 55 times on one test folder, across a reboot that landed during its writes, and left 56 settings.local.json.bak-pitstop-* files. Daily tuning (autotune.py) and setup.py prune to the newest three after each write; the hand-run path did not. (This row first said Pit Stop never removes backups; that was wrong.) The file itself came back whole each time.
rows.promise: A hand-run optimize.py --apply keeps the newest three backups of the settings file, as daily tuning and setup do.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, on a Mac, Claude Code 2.1.330, window 150K set by the tuner: Claude Code asked for an automatic compaction at 108,006 tokens with a file read of about 23K pending, before the context reached the window. The README said 'Above it, Claude Code wants to compact at once'.
rows.promise: The README says Claude Code asks to compact a little before the context reaches the window, gives that measurement as seen once, not as a promise, and never says 'at once'.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in that stress test, on a Linux laptop: a sudden reset cut a session in the middle of a 90-second Bash loop. The transcript ends on that tool_use with no result; on resume Claude Code shows 'No result recorded for 1 call' and 'Interrupted' and waits at an empty prompt. Pit Stop 0.6.1's PreCompact hook, run by hand on a copy of that transcript, answers hold (exit 2). Inferred and NOT seen: that Claude Code asks to compact such a session before a person types. On a macOS test machine on Claude Code 2.1.330, a session cut in the middle of a tool call by a clean reboot (not a sudden reset), leaving the same transcript shape, was resumed and waited three hours idle at an empty prompt, at 109K tokens with a 150K window and a 100K idle minimum, and was never asked.
rows.promise: A tool call with no result, made before the session's latest resume, counts as a break; a fresh start, /clear or a compaction never turns a running tool call into one. A guard for a case the transcript makes possible, not seen to occur on the Claude Code version tested.
rows.proven: Not seen on a real machine: on Claude Code 2.1.330 a resumed session cut in a tool call was not asked to compact in three hours idle (2026-11-22), so the hook was never called. What would count: a precompact.log line 'ALLOW break:cut-by-restart' from a real session, on any Claude Code version. This written reason does not hold 0.6.2 (accepted by the maintainers' reviewer, 2026-11-22).

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in clean test accounts with no GitHub key: on Claude Code 2.1.280 the README's catalog line and Pit Stop's install worked over HTTPS, but the catalog's 'github' entry for Windstorm Pit Board went straight to SSH and failed ('Host key verification failed'); 2.1.330 fell back to HTTPS. A plain https 'url' entry with the same ref and sha installed on both. 2026-11-23, Claude Code 2.1.280 on Linux, in a clean test account with no ssh-agent, no ~/.gitconfig and no ssh config: adding the catalog by its short name printed 'SSH not configured, cloning via HTTPS' and worked in all three states below, while installing the catalog's 'github' entry ran git over SSH (Claude Code set BatchMode=yes and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes) and failed in all three: with no key and no known_hosts, at the host key; with a key GitHub does not know and no known_hosts, at the host key; with that key and github.com's host keys in known_hosts, at the key ('Permission denied (publickey)'). Not seen: an account whose key GitHub knows. 2026-11-23, a stock Ubuntu 24.04.5 machine, Claude Code 2.1.330, no sign-in and no GitHub key (seen by Pit Board's maintainers before its pin moved): installing Pit Board's 'github' entry fell back to HTTPS and worked, but UPDATING it, after only its ref and sha moved in a copy of the catalog, went to SSH and failed ('No ED25519 host key is known for github.com … Host key verification failed'), and it stayed on the old version. So a person with no key can install a 'github' entry on 2.1.330 and never update it. Pit Stop's own installs from the './' entry updated over HTTP(S) on 2.1.280 and 2.1.330 (Linux and macOS).
rows.promise: Every install line in the README and every entry in the catalog works for a person with no GitHub account and no key, on the oldest Claude Code version the README names, and the README names that version. Seen in a clean account before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22: Pit Stop's catalog entry is './', so a fresh install on Claude Code 2.1.280 took main's commit 634d860d under the label 0.6.1, while the v0.6.1 tag is 36f536a1. A './' entry is copied to the cache, and the hooks run from the cache, never from the catalog clone, so a catalog refresh alone changes no running code (seen on Claude Code 2.1.280 and 2.1.330, on Linux and macOS). On Claude Code 2.1.280 (Linux) and 2.1.330 (macOS), with an orphaned cache folder labelled 0.6.1 from another commit present: a fresh install overwrote it, but an update from 0.1.4 to 0.6.1 reused it, so the registry named the new commit while the folder held the old commit's files (2026-11-22, clean test accounts; the same with a made-up plugin in a reduced reproduction on 2.1.280).
rows.promise: The catalog installs a released, tagged commit of Pit Stop, never main; each release is the tag first, then the pin on main, and the tests fail while a tag waits for its pin. Seen in a clean account before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22: changing Pit Stop's entry from './' to a pinned source changes the source of installs people already have (0.1.4 and 0.6.1 from './' exist on real machines). A catalog-only change did not move an existing install on Claude Code 2.1.330.
rows.promise: An install of 0.1.4 or 0.6.1 made from the './' entry reaches the pinned release with the README's own update lines, with no reinstall, and keeps pit-stop/config.json and the settings Pit Stop wrote. Seen on a real machine before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, a clean test account, Claude Code 2.1.280: with a stale cache folder labelled 0.6.1 from another commit present, 'claude plugin update' from 0.1.4 to 0.6.1 printed 'updated from 0.1.4 to 0.6.1', and installed_plugins.json named the new commit, but the folder held the old commit's files byte for byte. A fresh install overwrote such a folder. The same on Claude Code 2.1.330 (macOS, a clean test account): 3 of 51 files differed from the commit the registry named.
rows.promise: Every plugin update Pit Stop runs compares the cache folder's files with the commit the registry names. When they differ, Pit Stop reports it and stops there: it does not repair another program's cache by itself, and the line it prints gives the person the two commands that put it right (uninstall, then install, of that plugin at that scope). Seen on a real machine before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, a scratch branch: a real test was made unreachable four ways. The PROMISES gate and the plan check found tests by name in the text, and the PROMISES gate looked at a row only from its due version (the plan check not running in CI is row P15). The test used as the specimen runs and passes on main.
rows.promise: A codon's proof and a row's test count only if the runner collected and PASSED them in a whole-suite run, at any version; a partial run says so and checks nothing; there is no switch to turn the check off. Shown by breaking a real test in a scratch branch and seeing the run fail, before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, a scratch branch: a real test hidden by a later definition with the same name never ran, and every gate passed, including CI's invariant check (INV9), which caught the other three ways of making a test unreachable.
rows.promise: No test file defines the same top-level name twice, so no test can be hidden by another; a hidden test fails the run. Shown by breaking a real test in a scratch branch, before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22: the plan check (codon_check.py --strict --proofs tests), which ties each codon to its proof, ran only by hand; .github/workflows/tests.yml ran only pytest, so a codon whose proof was missing could merge.
rows.promise: Every gate that ties codons or rows to tests runs in CI on every pull request, and a pull request cannot merge while one of them fails. Seen in CI's checks on a pull request before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22: every place that states Pit Stop's version said 0.6.1 at the v0.6.1 tag and on main, but main had taken 28 more commits (5 files, 57 lines in hooks and scripts) under that label, and through the './' entry four different commits were installed as 0.6.1 on real and test machines. A sister plugin whose manifest named an old version saw 'claude plugin update' say 'already at the latest version' and keep the old code (Claude Code 2.1.330); not yet seen with Pit Stop.
rows.promise: One version names one release: the changelog's top release, plugin.json and Pit Stop's pinned catalog ref agree; every entry in the catalog has a ref that is a tag and a sha that is that tag's own commit; and no release ships new code under the last release's version. Held by a test in this repository.

rows.seen: 2026-11-23, one Linux box: a read-only probe that finds claude with shutil.which in a non-interactive ssh shell (PATH first, the rule Pit Stop's find_claude() uses) named a root-owned npm global copy, /usr/bin/claude 2.1.322, that nothing runs. The person's sessions run Anthropic's native install in ~/.local/share/claude/versions (2.1.309 and 2.1.319; newest 2.1.321), and ~/.claude.json says installMethod 'global'. Pit Stop's own code was read, not run, on that box.
rows.promise: Pit Stop names the Claude Code a person's sessions really run: what running sessions execute first, the person's login-shell PATH second, never a short PATH alone. A second install is named, not hidden, and when the two disagree Pit Stop says so plainly instead of choosing in silence. Seen on a real machine before the release that carries it is tagged.

rows.seen: 2026-11-22, in a signed-in conformance kit run on a Linux test account with Claude Code 2.1.280: the kit's session reached 25K tokens of a 100K window, so its hold and allow checks failed, and nothing told "the kit did not fill" from "Pit Stop failed". On 2026-11-23 the cause could no longer be read: the session's transcript was gone with the test account's cleanup.
rows.promise: The kit shows its own fill: its first check, fill, reads the session's own transcript and passes only when a model call's context reached the window; the session takes turns of new filler until precompact.log shows a HOLD and an ALLOW or the context stops growing; each turn's peak goes to an evidence file, numbers only, kept off the test account; a fill FAIL exits 3.

rows.seen: 2026-11-23, on a Linux test account with Claude Code 2.1.280: `claude plugin uninstall` emptied Pit Stop's row in the plugin registry but left its cache folder, marked `.orphaned_at`, and the launcher that fleet mode's timer runs picked that folder, so a person who had set up fleet mode and left by Claude Code's own uninstall would keep a timer running the uninstalled restart helper (restarts, typed notes) every 5 minutes. A sister plugin saw the same marker on a stock machine with 2.1.330.
rows.promise: Nothing runs once the plugin is gone: the launcher starts nothing and the restart helper changes no session when the folder carries `.orphaned_at`, when the registry reads fine and has no Pit Stop row, or when it cannot be read (that pass only); each pass says which in one line, with the command that takes the timer off when the plugin is gone; the checkup names an unreadable registry; after a plugin update the new folder runs.
rows.proven: 2026-11-23, on a stock Ubuntu 24.04.5 virtual machine with Claude Code 2.1.330 and no sign-in, from this row's code at the pull request's head 0b06cc6 (scripts/ there differs from the merged release branch only in gone_line(), which a timer's run through the launcher does not reach): fleet setup installed the timer; after Claude Code's own `claude plugin uninstall`, the timer's next passes started nothing and logged that Pit Stop is not installed, with `systemctl --user disable --now pit-stop-restart.timer`; that command, run as printed, exited 0 and the timer was gone. Installing the same version again cleared `.orphaned_at` and the helper ran again. Also on a Linux test account with Claude Code 2.1.280: the marker was cleared on the same-version reinstall, twice. Not seen on macOS (no command is printed there).

rows.seen: 2026-11-24, walking setup, leaving and setup again in a throwaway home: with no Pit Stop row in Claude Code's plugin list (a copy run with --plugin-dir, or setup again after `claude plugin uninstall`), `/pit-stop setup --fleet --apply` wrote the launcher, restart.json and the timer, said "enabled and started" and answered 0, while the launcher that timer runs said on every pass "nothing run: Pit Stop is not installed". Released 0.6.1's setup makes no such check.
rows.promise: With --fleet, setup checks first and last what the timer's own launcher checks. With no Pit Stop row it makes and changes nothing of fleet mode, names a timer an earlier install left (it runs nothing until Pit Stop is installed again), says fleet mode is NOT set up with the one install command, and answers 1. It says "fleet mode is set up" and answers 0 only when the launcher finds Pit Stop. A plugin list that cannot be read is "not checked", with no advice to set up again.
